Paper_Metadata.Paper_Title: The impact of surface orientation on surface roughness and fatigue life of laser-based powder bed fusion Ti-6Al-4V

0° (No-HIP): YS 1093 ± 7.5 MPa, UTS 1226 ± 3 MPa, Max. Elongation 2.09 ± 0.7%

Nominal_Composition.Note: Commercial Ti-6Al-4V designation reported; no explicit numerical composition was provided in the paper.

Process_Text.original: Fatigue and tensile specimens were produced using LB-PBF (SLM Solutions 250) with Ti-6Al-4V powder. Before using virgin Ti-6Al-4V powder, two drying runs were completed to remove any moisture present. After drying, the powder is sieved (~100µm) resulting in a Dv90 powder size distribution of 65.8 µm and Dv50 of 44.5 µm. Applied process parameters are: 30 µm layer height, 100 W laser power, 425 mm/s scan speed on borders and 375 mm/s scan speed on hatching. Fatigue specimens dimensions conform to subsize specimens in ASTM E466 and tensile specimens conform to subsize specimens specified in ASTM E8. Fatigue specimens were manufactured at six inclination angles from 90° down to 0°. Specimens manufactured at or above 40° did not require supports in the gauge section, only on the lower grip section. Specimens manufactured below 40° required supports for the gauge section. The support method adopted a thin-wall, edge support in contact with the perimeter of the gauge section and column supports separated by 100 µm from the downward-facing surface of the specimen gauge section to avoid mutual contact, thus no machining was required and an as-manufactured surface was achieved. No HIP was applied to this specimen group.
Process_Text.simplified: Ti-6Al-4V 0° specimens built by LB-PBF on SLM Solutions 250. Powder Dv50=44.5 µm, Dv90=65.8 µm. Process: 30 µm layer, 100 W laser, 425 mm/s border scan, 375 mm/s hatching. As-manufactured surface, no HIP. Tensile specimens per ASTM E8 subsize.

Structure_Text.original: The α′ martensite, typical of LB-PBF Ti-6Al-4V, is observed before HIP. Needle-like alpha laths are observed within the prior beta grains; prior beta grains exhibit epitaxial growth parallel to the build direction of the specimens. Backscatter and EBSD images of vertically built 90° specimens before HIP were used to approximate average lath statistics.
Structure_Text.simplified: Before HIP, as-manufactured LB-PBF Ti-6Al-4V shows α′ martensite with needle-like alpha laths inside prior beta grains. Prior beta grains grow epitaxially parallel to the build direction.

Secondary_Phases.Note: Needle-like alpha laths within prior beta grains; typical of LB-PBF Ti-6Al-4V before HIP

Process_Text.original: Same LB-PBF process as other specimens (SLM Solutions 250) with Ti-6Al-4V powder. Process parameters: 30 µm layer height, 100 W laser power, 425 mm/s scan speed on borders and 375 mm/s scan speed on hatching. 0° inclination angle. HIP applied: 820 °C, 200 MPa, 2 h hold time in pure argon atmosphere. All specimens were ultrasonically cleaned using de-ionised water prior to HIP to remove loose powder. As-manufactured surface.
Process_Text.simplified: Ti-6Al-4V 0° specimens built by LB-PBF, then HIP at 820 °C / 200 MPa / 2 h in pure argon. As-manufactured surface retained.

Structure_Text.original: The effect of grain coarsening after HIP is visually evident in the backscatter and EBSD images. Based on approximations derived from EBSD data in vertically built 90° specimens before and after HIP, using equivalent ellipse fitting method, after HIP, the lath length and breadth increase by approximately two times. Approximate average lath statistics for specimens manufactured at 0° after HIP show that the average length and breadth is larger in the bulk region by less than 7%. The average lath area is larger in the bulk region by less than 19%. In regions close to the side and downward-facing surfaces, columnar growth of prior-beta grains parallel to build direction is not obvious. However, clear bands of similarly oriented laths can be seen within columnar prior beta grains in the bulk region.
Structure_Text.simplified: HIP causes lath coarsening; lath area, length and breadth approximately double. Bulk region has slightly larger laths than edge region (length/breadth <7% larger, area <19% larger). Columnar prior-beta growth is less obvious near surfaces.

Secondary_Phases.Note: Needle-like alpha laths coarsened by HIP treatment within prior beta grains

Structure_Text.original: After HIP, average lath length for 30° specimens is less than for 0° and 90° in both bulk and edge regions. Average lath breadth for 30° specimens is greater than 0° and 90° specimens in the bulk region. In regions close to the side and downward-facing surfaces, columnar growth of prior-beta grains parallel to build direction is not obvious. Clear bands of similarly oriented laths can be seen within columnar prior beta grains in the bulk region.
Structure_Text.simplified: HIP-treated 30° specimens show shorter but broader laths compared to 0° and 90°. Columnar prior-beta growth less obvious near surfaces.

Process_Text.original: LB-PBF Ti-6Al-4V with HIP at 820 °C, 200 MPa, 2 h in pure argon. Fatigue specimens at 0°, 10°, 30°, 50°, 70°, 90° inclination. Fully tensile uniaxial fatigue testing with R=0.1, f=20 Hz, runout at 1.5E6 cycles. 96 total fatigue tests. Either upward or downward-facing surface was polished.
Process_Text.simplified: LB-PBF Ti-6Al-4V, HIP-treated, fatigue tested at R=0.1, 20 Hz, 6 inclination angles, 96 total tests.

Structure_Text.original: After HIP, lath coarsening observed. Failure initiated at rough as-manufactured surface in almost all cases. Failure commonly originated at or near corners due to geometry-induced stress concentration.
Structure_Text.simplified: Post-HIP microstructure. Fatigue failure initiated at rough as-manufactured surfaces, typically near corners.
